messages:
mia: hitting a repro where our Rust SSE client emits partial JSON -> serde errors. stream chunks split inside multibyte utf8 and inside objects. any quick patterns folks use to avoid parse failures + keep backpressure sane?

sasha: short answer: accumulate bytes and only attempt parse when you see a full delimiter (we use ndjson "
"). also watch utf8 boundaries with BytesMut::split_to so you don't corrupt sequences.

mia: thanks — we're not currently using ndjson. upstream sends `data: {...}

` framed SSE messages. the problem is bursts: tokio tasks queue up and memory spikes.

kevin: two quick levers: 1) apply bounded mpsc channel between reader -> parser so readers await when parser is overloaded; 2) use serde_json::StreamDeserializer so you can feed partial slices and it yields values as they finish. example: `let mut de = Deserializer::from_slice(&buf).into_iter::<Value>();` then drain parsed items and keep remainder bytes.

jen: for SSE specifically, we also add a simple state machine: collect until `

` (SSE event end) then strip `data: ` prefixes and feed into parser. If queue length > N, slow down the socket consumer by awaiting the bounded sender. avoids unbounded mem growth.

mia: any tips on handling token refresh + streaming reconnect? we sometimes hit 401 mid-stream and restart which doubles peak memory when reconnects overlap.

kevin: cancel the old reader future immediately on 401 before spinning up a new one. using a cancellation token (tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken) works well. also debounce reconnect attempts so you don't have multiple concurrent connects.

sasha: also consider incremental UTF-8 safety: when slicing a buffer keep the last up to 4 bytes as potential partial char and prepend to next chunk. BytesMut::split_to helps here.

jen: if parse latency matters, try simd-json for parse speed + lower queue; otherwise serde streaming + bounded queue is simplest.

mia: ps — added tiny repro in playground: `read_to_end -> push to bounded tx -> parser task tries StreamDeserializer, on Err store leftover bytes and continue`. will post gist in thread. thanks y'all :heart: :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Related doc: https://redwood.internal/devex/streaming-best-practices (archived notes on bounded queues, SSE framing, reconnect strategies)

kevin: one last nit — if you accept partial JSON fragments from multiple SSE events, make sure to join with a separator or validate merging rules. accidental concatenation can create valid but wrong JSON. prefer explicit event-level objects.

mia: great, I'll try bounded mpsc + cancellation token + safe utf8 slicing first. will follow up with a short PR.
